title: Collapsable filters for mobile

comments.body: @Maaark thanks for sharing you're use case. It seems that you are changing the content of the dom generated by the instant search widget (l.696 of algolia.js for example), and this will mess with the internal React rendering. If you change the outer dom it should be ok though.
@bobylito What do you mean exactly with the outerdom? What element? Since we need to have a specific structure in order to have collapse functionality
I use "outer DOM" as opposed to the DOM that's inside the widget. If you create DOM wrappers that fits the rules for your scripts that would work.
But the issue is that I need to alter the react generated html to give it the right structure for the collapse functionality.
Actually, there is an option to make the refinement list widget collapse already built-in. https://community.algolia.com/instantsearch.js/documentation/#refinementlist Would that work for you?

@bobylito I tried that one but it didn't work. I reapplied it now, so you can see that it's not working and perhaps find the bug.

To make it a bit more complicated, we want to show the minimalized version only to devices with a window width < 600px. Bigger sizes should get our current version, with all options visible. Is that something we can do?
@bobylito Can you confirm to me that it's a bug or did we do something wrong?
I will make a proper example to test and check the behaviour and see if we're on the same page.
Hi @Maaark if you experienced any issue while using the collapsable option can you please demonstrate it somehow then we can work on it? Thanks

@vvo You can see what I mean at https://markputs.nl/algolia.php. Make your screen 400px, click at filter resultaten and all of those refinement lists are collapsable: true. See for example that Merken area.

And is it possible to make the collapsable functionality work with predefined window width limits? So for example we want to be the refinement lists only collapsable when the window width is < 768px?
@bobylito @vvo Any idea when you guys can have a look at this?
It's an old issue and we haven't encountered it again. Please reopen an issue if you're experiencing it again.
